text:
jordan: Heads up — procurement forwarded a vendor note: H100 replacement batch ETA pushed from 2026-05-07 -> 2026-05-21. Vendor flags this as "thermal-transport" and wants to add an insurance premium of 3.5% of declared value for air shipments. This could add ~USD 12k per AWB and impacts APAC RMA timing. AWB listed below. Thoughts?

maria: yep saw it. vendor says recent carrier rate changes + thermal handling liability triggered the premium. they gave two options: (1) vendor-validated air with insurance at 3.5% or (2) move to sea (no premium) but +14 days on transit. pricing impact: per-air-insurance = `~$12,000` for batch value `~$350k`.

cheng: What are SLA consequences if we pick sea? our customer promise for replacements is 10 business days in APAC right now. Sea would blow that. any local depot spares we can pull from?

maria: short answer: sea pushes to ~20-28 days total door. we have ~6 H100s in redeployable pool (EU/Dedicated) but none staged in SG right now. finance would prefer sea+no premium but ops might lose SLA.

elyse: SG customs flagged thermal units last month — if not shipped under certified thermal docs they go to inspection and get held for 48-72h. carrier is asking for thermal-certificate + augmented insurance to cover temp damage in handling. we can avoid some risk by adding an on-arrival depot inspection step (photo evidence + ATP).

dan: proposal: spin up loaner pool for affected clusters for 2-3 weeks, accept sea for replacements to save cost, and concurrently push vendor to absorb part of insurance. where do we pull loaners from? can we hot-swap from non-prod?

jordan: good pragmatic plan. Need a quick decision: accept premium and keep air (meets SLA but +$12k), or go sea + loaners (meet cost targets but need loaner ops). Can we split shipment? e.g., send 30% air insured (urgent nodes), rest by sea?

ops-bot: Ticket created: INF-7283 — APAC RMA routing + insurance negotiation. Assignees: maria, elyse.

maria: I can negotiate split: vendor says they will accept split if we cover customs variance and partial insurance. I'll push vendor to reduce premium to 2% if we commit to a 50/50 split. If vendor won't budge, we'll ask finance for one-off cover for insurance for priority units.

cheng: to enable loaners: list of candidate serials I can hot-swap from non-prod: `SN-H100-0421`, `SN-H100-0423`, `SN-H100-0440`. Depot contact in SG is Sam Lee (sam.lee@3pl.example). Sam can prebook inspection slot on arrival to avoid extra hold.

elyse: I'll reach Sam and book a slot for the 30% air tranche. Also pushing local forwarder to confirm thermal docs. If we go air for priority, we should manifest these as "replacement-critical" to reduce handling touch.

maria: OK plan: (A) negotiate premium down to 2% for split shipments, (B) provision 3 loaners from non-prod for 2-3 weeks, (C) schedule depot inspection for air tranche. I'll update INF-7283 with vendor response by EOD PST.

dan: @maria @cheng i'll start prepping hot-swap runbook and tag machines for loaner. @jordan once you confirm which clusters get priority air we can lock AWBs.

jordan: sounds good. prioritize edge-prod clusters in APAC first. do the split, negotiate, and prep loaners. :thumbsup:
